behaviors.description: Require every nonblank line to be a JSON object containing exactly the fields key and delta, where key is a string and delta is an integer but not a boolean.

observables: Objects missing key or delta are rejected
Objects with extra fields are rejected
Arrays, scalars, malformed JSON, non-string keys, floats, strings, nulls, and boolean deltas are rejected

behaviors.description: Sum all accepted delta values independently by their key, including negative and repeated deltas.
source_refs: Raw requirements: sum deltas by key
observables: Repeated keys produce one total
Different keys remain independent

behaviors.description: On valid input, emit exactly one compact JSON object whose keys are lexicographically sorted, followed by exactly one newline.

observables: Output contains no spaces introduced by JSON separators
Key ordering is lexicographic
Empty input emits '{}\n'
Successful output is valid JSON and has exactly one trailing newline

behaviors.description: For any specified invalid input, emit no stdout, emit one concise stderr line, and exit with status 2, even when invalid data follows valid records.

observables: Exit status is exactly 2
Stdout is empty
Stderr consists of one concise newline-terminated line
No partial aggregate is emitted before the entire input has been validated

failure_modes.description: Duplicate JSON member names may be collapsed by the decoder, allowing a source object with repeated key or delta members to pass the exactly-two-fields check.
observable_signals: Only the last duplicate member value affects the aggregate

failure_modes.description: A syntactically valid JSON integer exceeding the runtime's integer-string conversion limit can raise an uncaught ValueError, producing a traceback and exit status 1 instead of the required one-line error and status 2.
observable_signals: Very long integer input exits with status other than 2
Stderr contains a Python traceback or multiple lines
required_capabilities: Submit an extremely long JSON integer

failure_modes.description: UTF-8 decoding depends on the process stdin text encoding; under a non-UTF-8 runtime configuration, valid UTF-8 input could be rejected or decoded incorrectly.
observable_signals: Behavior changes with locale or Python UTF-8 mode
Valid non-ASCII UTF-8 bytes produce an encoding error
required_capabilities: Run the program under alternate locale/runtime encoding settings

failure_modes.description: A key containing an escaped lone surrogate can pass string validation but fail during UTF-8 output encoding, causing no valid result and an uncontrolled error.
observable_signals: Input with a key such as "\ud800" terminates abnormally
No required JSON output line is produced
required_capabilities: Submit JSON containing an escaped lone surrogate
Observe stdout, stderr, and exit status

failure_modes.description: The automated tests do not probe duplicate-member semantics, parser resource-limit exceptions, locale-dependent decoding, or escaped-surrogate output failures.
observable_signals: All five current tests pass while F1 through F4 remain possible
No test cases contain duplicate object members, extremely long integers, alternate locales, or escaped lone surrogates
required_capabilities: Inspect or run the test suite

failure_modes.description: Deeply nested or otherwise pathological JSON can raise exceptions such as RecursionError that bypass the controlled error path, resulting in a traceback and the wrong exit status.
observable_signals: Pathological input exits with status other than 2

Repository evidence and producer evidence are authored from the same project tests and documentation, creating correlated omissions; repeatedly passing the declared five-test suite cannot independently expose absent edge classes.

The two agentic reviewers and the adversarial test agent share source/runtime context and closely related Codex-generated adversarial reasoning, so their chosen limits and fixtures may converge on the same cases.
